solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Difficult screening start of horror film

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the difficult word is wrapped round the next letter

parts.note: a testing time is a difficult one

indicators.note: start of takes only the opening letter of the word horror

explanation.surface: A cinema showing the opening of a horror film is hard to sit through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' puts H, the first letter of 'horror', inside TESTING. THE STING is the 1973 Newman and Redford caper film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sting is an Oscar-winning 1973 con-artist movie, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Swell reaching great volume?

parts.note: to means as far as, reaching
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A wave swells until it reaches a huge volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests a book or quantity; it is loudness in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is old slang for a posh, fashionable person, the same as a toff.

clue.text: Noble and tragic figure with head lowered

indicators.note: in a down clue the head is the top letter, and lowering it moves it to the bottom

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic hero

explanation.surface: An aristocratic tragic hero bows his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head lowered' moves L, the first letter of LEAR, to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Where Parisians stroll in leisure time, half drunk

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and muddled, so the letters are jumbled
half takes the first two of the four letters of time

explanation.surface: Parisians take a walk in their free time, already half cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' gives TI from TIME; 'drunk' mixes LEISURE plus TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuileries Garden in central Paris is a public park popular for walks.

clue.text: Brass tacks and polish quickly put away in raised floor

indicators.note: in sets the polishing and eating words inside the other piece
in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the floor word goes backwards

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them down or stun them
to sand is to smooth or polish
to bolt food is to eat it fast

explanation.surface: Brass fittings and polish are swiftly tidied away under a raised floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is a verb here, to knock down; 'raised' reverses it because this is a down clue. 'Brass tacks' is the definition, not part of the surface's hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the practical basics, the nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Occult specialist withdrawing here in Rome

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the specialist word is read backwards

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert or specialist
hic is Latin, the language of ancient Rome, for here

explanation.surface: An expert in the occult is pulling out of their post in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here in Rome' asks for the Latin word, HIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphic means mystical or esoteric, after the mystery cult of Orpheus, so it suits occult.

clue.text: Snub pariah the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means backwards, so the outcast word is reversed

parts.note: a leper is an outcast or pariah

explanation.surface: Ignoring an outcast is the wrong way to behave.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub is to rebuff, which is to repel someone's approach.

clue.text: E.g. Louis Armstrong, a hero in the main

definitions.meaning: Armstrong was a jazz trumpeter, a player of a horn
Horatio ... is C S Forester's naval hero on the high seas

explanation.surface: Satchmo is cast as a hero of the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter blows a horn; Hornblower is the fictional Royal Navy captain of Forester's novels.

clue.text: Urban area cryptically suggesting it?

parts.note: the centre of the word city is the pair of letters spelling it

explanation.surface: An urban area hints at itself cryptically.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the middle of CITY is IT, the clue's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A city centre is the downtown core of a town, an urban district.

clue.text: Link breaking on birthday

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the link word is set inside the other piece

parts.note: to go on is to go forth
a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: A connection snaps on someone's birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a piece, not a link word: to go on is to go forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortieth is a fortieth birthday, the celebration of turning forty, in casual usage.

clue.text: Drive back from Mumbai in journeys westward

indicators.note: in says the Mumbai letter goes inside the other piece
in an across clue westward means right to left, so the journeys word reads backwards

parts.note: trips are journeys

indicators.note: back from takes the final letter of the word Mumbai

explanation.surface: A drive back from Mumbai is part of a trip heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward' turns TRIPS into SPIRT; 'in' puts I, the last letter of Mumbai ('back from'), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit means energy and determination, the same as drive in a person.

clue.text: A single amount of DNA that I'm allotted?

definitions.text: A single amount of DNA that I'm allotted?

parts.words: A single amount of DNA that I'm allotted?
parts.note: read whimsically as one person's allotted share of a single unit of heredity; the whole is a 1965 song title by The Who

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how much genetic material they personally receive.
explanation.walkthrough: Break the answer as MY GENE RATION: my share of a gene. It is also The Who's 1965 hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who song title, read whimsically as one's allotted portion of genetic code.

clue.text: Winter time basically represented in iambic pentameter?

parts.note: Dec is short for December, a winter month

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the letters of basically are reordered

explanation.surface: The winter season, put simply, rendered in Shakespearean verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges BASICALLY to ASYLLABIC. The question mark flags that iambic pentameter is just one example of ten-syllable lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambic pentameter line has five two-syllable feet, ten syllables in all, so it is decasyllabic.

clue.text: Wrongly catching the setter's back, removing coat

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the setter's word reads upwards

parts.note: the setter's is short for the setter is, I'm
shearing removes a sheep's fleece, its coat

explanation.surface: The setter's back is clipped as the jacket comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishearing is catching words wrongly, as in hearing them incorrectly.

clue.text: Tinned meat, diced, being kept in the can

definitions.note: a gerund phrase standing for the noun

indicators.note: diced means chopped up, so the letters are cut and shuffled

explanation.surface: Chopped canned meat is stored in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the can' is slang for prison, not a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Detainment is confinement; the can is slang for jail.

clue.text: Cooler part of UK for Briton once

definitions.note: the answer names a tribe; one member is meant

parts.note: ice cools drinks, so it is a cooler
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Which colder region of Britain would an ancient Briton choose?
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were Boudicca's tribe in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic tribe of ancient Britain, so they are early Britons.

clue.text: Choose casual look for carpet

definitions.meaning: to carpet someone is to scold them, also to dress them down

explanation.surface: Pick an informal outfit to wear over the floor covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet as a verb is British slang for a reprimand, as when a boss calls you in on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress down covers both informal clothing and giving someone a stern telling-off.

clue.text: Lefty hasn't succeeded, English party stalwart

indicators.note: hasn't says the succeeded letter is dropped

parts.note: a socialist is on the political left
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A left-winger who failed is a loyal party member in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political; it is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialite is a fixture of fashionable social events, so a dependable partygoer.

clue.text: Grave details conveyed by this teacher's voice

parts.note: a head is a head teacher, so the head's
a tone of voice

explanation.surface: A teacher's tone conveys solemn details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like serious; it is the burial plot whose details a headstone bears.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone records the name and dates of the person buried in the grave.

clue.text: Pull in net

definitions.meaning: to earn or pull it in as profit
... profit is net profit, what remains after costs

explanation.surface: Haul a catch in a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear as verb means earn after deductions, and as adjective means net of expenses.

clue.text: Wife associated with Avon hair dye rejected a new hat fashion

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the dye word reads backwards

parts.note: henna is a reddish hair dye

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of hat are rearranged

parts.note: a way is a manner or fashion of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone refuses hair dye and a fresh style of hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Avon is the river through Stratford, Shakespeare's town; 'fashion' means manner, not style of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hathaway married Shakespeare, the Bard of Avon from Stratford-upon-Avon.

clue.text: Poet using some cliché in expression

indicators.note: using some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet resorts to a cliché when expressing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was a nineteenth-century German lyric writer of verse.

clue.text: Uncovered base ingredient in perfume

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters off the base word

parts.note: the bottom is the base

explanation.surface: A base note of a perfume has been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' removes B and M from BOTTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, or attar, is a fragrant oil from rose petals used in scent.

clue.text: Jog or run through school

indicators.note: through says the run letter passes inside the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Jogging or running round the school grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to nudge or prod them.

clue.text: I live by inlet in peninsula

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a ria is a drowned river valley forming a coastal inlet

explanation.surface: Someone lives beside a coastal inlet on a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian Peninsula holds Spain and Portugal, so Iberia is that land mass.

clue.text: One is found in church, perhaps

definitions.text: One is found in church, perhaps

indicators.note: is found in puts the numeral inside the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large church, so perhaps flags an example
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A clergyman is the sort of person you would meet in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: I inside MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a clergyman who leads worship, typically found in church.

clue.text: Nearly go out in Germany's capital, say

indicators.note: capital means the leading letter, so the first letter of Germany is taken

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Almost going out in Berlin, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Berlin; it is the capital letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle gutters when its flame flickers and nearly dies, just short of going out.

clue.text: Registered where the needle goes

definitions.meaning: a gramophone needle sits on a record

explanation.definitionFit: Something put on record is formally documented; a stylus plays a vinyl disc by riding on it.
